create.title: Limit loan renewals
create.description: Members may renew a loan at most twice, so popular items come back into circulation and waiting members get a fair chance.

steps.markdown:
# Limit loan renewals
A loan can be renewed while nobody has reserved the item. Today that works forever, so one member can keep a popular DVD for months. Allow two renewals per loan and explain the refusal on the third attempt.

data.problem: A member can renew the same loan indefinitely while nobody reserves the item.
data.desiredBehavior: Allow at most two renewals per loan and reject the third with a clear message.
data.nonGoals: No change to reservation rules, fees or loan durations.
data.constraints: Renewals blocked by a reservation keep their current error.
data.assumptions: Renewal counts start at zero for loans created before this change.

entities.label: Requirement
entities.title: Two renewals per loan
entities.content: A loan can be renewed at most two times.

entities.label: Requirement
entities.title: Clear refusal
entities.content: The third renewal is rejected with a RuleViolation that names the limit.

entities.label: AcceptanceCriterion
entities.title: Two renewals succeed
entities.content: A loan without reservations can be renewed twice, each time extending the due date by the item's loan days.

entities.label: AcceptanceCriterion
entities.title: Third renewal fails
entities.content: Given a loan renewed twice, renewing again returns HTTP 409 with 'Renewal limit reached'.

entities.label: TestCase
entities.title: Renew twice, then refuse
entities.content: Borrow a book, renew twice successfully, expect the third renewal to throw RuleViolation.
entities.reason: Directly proves the new two-renewal limit from REQ-001 and AC-001.

entities.label: TestCase
entities.title: Reservation still blocks renewal
entities.content: With a waiting reservation, the first renewal already fails with the existing message.
entities.reason: Guards the existing reservation rule so the new limit does not replace it.

steps.markdown:
# Source analysis
CirculationService.renew extends dueAt by the item's loan days after checking the reservation queue. Loan has no counter yet. LibraryController does not expose renewals, so only the service changes.

data.facts: CirculationService.renew checks ReservationService.queueLength and then extends Loan.dueAt.
data.approximations: Static calls show the renewal path; runtime usage is not measured.
data.inferences: A renewCount on Loan is the smallest place to hold the limit.
data.risks: Loans saved before the change have no counter and must default to zero.
data.testRationale: TC-002 guards the existing reservation rule while the new limit is added.

entities.label: TestCase
entities.title: Legacy loan starts at zero renewals
entities.content: A loan created without renewCount can still be renewed twice.
entities.reason: Analysis found loans are stored without a counter today, so old loans must default to zero.

steps.markdown:
# Keep the rule in the service
Loan stores the counter; CirculationService enforces the limit next to the existing reservation check. No new class.

data.responsibilities: Loan records renewCount; CirculationService enforces the limit.
data.interfaces: renew(loanId) keeps its signature and return type.
data.errorHandling: RuleViolation('Renewal limit reached') maps to HTTP 409 like other rule violations.
data.testability: FixedClock and in-memory repositories cover the rule without I/O.
data.alternatives: A RenewalPolicy class would add indirection for a single constant.
data.simplicity: One field and one guard clause.

entities.label: ArchitectureDecision
entities.title: Enforce the limit in CirculationService
entities.content: The renewal limit sits next to the reservation check in CirculationService.renew; Loan only stores the count.

judgment.rationale: Smallest change that keeps rules in one service.

steps.markdown:
# Plan
Implement the counter and guard, then add the two test cases.

data.strategy: Add renewCount to Loan, guard CirculationService.renew, extend tests/circulation.test.ts.
data.dependencies: Tests follow the implementation in the same task.
